# the contributor audit: fixed-body optimality does not remove inside facets

Source: `candidate b328374adbd9cb3e`.
Full read: PASS. the contributor reran 1,206 exact checks. The all-normal body certificate
is unchanged from the already independently audited example.

The inverse affine tilt F(a)=sum zV_z/(1+az) is strictly decreasing and has
opposite infinite endpoint limits. Its isolated algebraic root is therefore
unique in the entire positive-parameter domain, not just the isolating
interval. The displayed rational numerator identity and signs are checked.

For t_z=1+alpha z the root gives sum V_z/t_z=M exactly. Thus rho=dm/(Mt_z)
is a probability with full barycenter at the proposed mark and L moment
L_0=s. Its original-volume tilt is dm/M. Direct Jensen then proves, for every
positive normalized concave U,

    U(Y)/s >= mean_m(U/L) >= exp(mean_m log(U/L))=1.

After rescaling epsilon, the source buffer is precisely the already audited
one. Every other base retains an upper bound from pure-base caps below Q,
and within the source fiber the constant value of L preserves strict energy
maximality at the centroid. Global fixed-body optimality follows. Equality
requires U(Y)=s by proper-gap strictness, and then strict logarithmic Jensen
requires U=L on every sampled fiber. This is uniqueness of sampled values,
not of arbitrary unsampled concave extensions.

The normal zonoid construction is exact for every inside allocation: reflect
it onto the equal-width core of the outside facet and allocate 1/4 on the
two excess strips. The proper-section first moment cancels the strips, giving
the stated full vector identity, including the continuous coordinate. It is
not merely a scalar width comparison or a finite sample of allocations.

Consequently the example simultaneously has unique global fixed-body
parameter optimality, a full contact martingale, the full facet zonoid
condition, and unavoidable inside-facet critical caps. It is above the OC
target and makes no joint body-minimality claim. The attempted rescue of
inside-free selection by fixed-body optimality alone is therefore false.
